Window types / W-04

Fixed windows

Glass that does not open, in a frame as wide as a casement. Choose it over a picture window when it sits beside opening units and the glass lines should match.

Estimate online Request a quote
Operation
Does not open
Frame depth
82.6 mm · 3 1/4"
Frame edge to glass
77.6 mm · 3 1/16"
Glass
Dual or triple pane
Profile section

How it is built

A fixed unit sets the glass directly in a wide welded frame: about 3 1/16" from the edge of the frame to the glass, the same as our casement and awning.

The glass is set from the room side and held by a glazing bead, so it can be replaced without taking the frame out.

Where it fits

  • Beside or between casements, so every pane is the same size
  • Rows of matching units across a wide opening
  • Anywhere a picture window would look too slim next to its neighbours

Glass

  • Double or triple pane sealed units
  • Low-E coatings, argon fill
  • Warm-edge spacer bars
  • Tempered glass where code requires it
  • Obscure / frosted glass for bathrooms
  • Internal grilles in several patterns

Frame & hardware

  • White, or laminated exterior colours and woodgrains
  • Multi-point locking hardware
  • Integrated screens
  • Brickmould, jamb extensions and nailing fin to suit your wall
  • Custom sizes and shapes

Other window types

W-01

Casement

Side-hinged, cranks open outward. The tightest seal of any opening window.
W-02

Awning

Top-hinged, opens outward from the bottom. Can stay open in the rain.
W-03

Picture

Fixed glass in the narrowest frame. The most light and the best insulation value.
